messages.content: Can we do one final logistics pass for Chicago? The app now says badge pickup opens Monday at 4:00 and Tuesday sessions start at 9:00. Forecast looks stormy and hot.

Yes. Monday: get to ATL about 2 hours before the late-morning ORD nonstop, a little earlier if you check a bag. At ORD, compare taxi and rideshare before leaving baggage claim; with storms and the city event, the taxi line may be steadier than surge pricing. If the room is not ready, leave luggage with the bell desk, pick up the badge after 4:00, then keep dinner near or inside the hotel.
Breakfast is still not included, correct?

Correct: the hotel has on-site dining, but breakfast is paid. Use a modest cafe or hotel breakfast only if the conference does not provide one, and save itemized receipts rather than only the card slip.
What should I do Monday night for Tuesday morning?

Walk the route from the elevator or lobby to the Tuesday meeting area after badge pickup. Also note the closest coffee option and where taxis or rideshares load, so Tuesday morning is just breakfast, badge, and the 9:00 session.
Any seat check left? We had window seats held.

Only a no-fee recheck. I cannot see the live seat map from here, so check the airline app after ticketing and again at check-in. If a better free window opens, take it; I would not pay just to move closer to the front.
Give me the day-before list.

Day before: confirm both flights still show nonstop; check weather waivers, gate, and seat map; screenshot boarding pass, hotel address, and confirmation; verify the quiet-room note; pack umbrella plus a light indoor layer; confirm badge pickup location; create one email folder for airline, hotel, conference, and receipt photos.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: casual dinners are easy with a kid

messages.content: Chicago is behind me. I want to start the St. Pete Beach family trip before school starts. Tentative window is Wednesday August 5 to Sunday August 9, but my spouse may only be able to take Thursday and Friday. Three of us from ATL. I want simple flights into Tampa or Sarasota, a Sunday return that doesn't wreck Monday, and a hotel or condo setup where beach, pool, breakfast or groceries, and casual dinners are easy with a kid.

The big forks are date, airport, and lodging. Wed-Sun gives more beach time but costs another night and more PTO; Thu-Sun is cleaner for work but makes flight timing matter more. Tampa should have the strongest ATL nonstop schedule and fares, with a 35-50 minute transfer to St. Pete Beach. Sarasota can shorten the drive a bit, but often has fewer flights and higher fares. Gulf-side lodging makes beach, pool, and dinner easiest; an inland suite helps with breakfast, parking, and space but turns beach time into a car routine.
If Wednesday only works after work, does it add enough?

Probably not unless the flight lands early enough to check in and get dinner without stress. A Wednesday evening arrival after 9 would add cost and a tired night. If a Thursday morning flight gets you to Florida before lunch, that may be the cleaner choice.
Is Sarasota worth paying more for?

Only if the times and fares are close. For St. Pete Beach, SRQ can reduce the drive, but not enough to justify an awkward schedule or a connection. TPA wins if it has nonstops and a sane Sunday return. SRQ is a backup if Tampa times are bad.
For lodging, I don't want us loading the car just to touch the beach every day.

Then the Gulf-side property gets the edge. For a short trip, walking from room to sand and pool can be worth more than included breakfast. The inland suite is better if the room is much larger, the savings are substantial, or a kitchenette matters enough to accept daily drives.
The resort has fees and paid breakfast. The suite has breakfast and parking included but is 15 minutes inland.

That's the core tradeoff. Resort: higher all-in rate, but simpler days and walkable dinners. Suite: cheaper mornings and more space, but likely rental car, beach parking, and time in and out. If you choose the resort, solve mornings with a grocery stop or delivery, a mini-fridge, and one or two cafe breakfasts.
Would you rent a car?

If you stay Gulf-side, price airport transfer or rideshare first and skip a full-trip rental unless you plan day trips. If you stay inland, rent a car; otherwise beach access gets annoying. Either way, check the booster-seat plan and whether the hotel charges parking.
What do I need to confirm with my spouse before I compare actual prices?

Ask: 1) can everyone leave Thursday morning, or is Wednesday truly possible; 2) is beach-walk convenience worth accepting paid breakfast and resort fees; 3) are balcony and kitchenette must-haves or just bonuses; 4) are you planning off-beach outings that require a car; 5) maximum all-in nightly budget after fees. Missing until then: exact flight times, cancellation terms, resort fee details, and whether the room has a fridge.

messages.content: Spouse confirmed Thursday August 6 through Sunday August 9; adding Monday is not happening. The best flights I'm seeing are ATL-TPA nonstop Thursday morning, or a cheaper after-work nonstop. Sarasota is about $90 to $120 more per person and the times are less convenient. Hotels are down to a Gulf-side pool property with nearby restaurants, resort fee and paid breakfast, or an inland suite about 15 minutes from the beach with breakfast and parking included. Which combo would you pick?

I would pick ATL-TPA nonstop Thursday morning, the late-afternoon TPA-ATL nonstop Sunday, and the Gulf-side property on a cancellable rate. For only three nights, the morning outbound protects the first beach afternoon, and the Gulf-side hotel keeps pool, sand, and casual dinners easy. This does mean accepting paid breakfast, but the beach convenience saves more time than the suite's included breakfast does. I would not pay extra for Sarasota here unless Tampa times change.
Talk me out of the cheaper after-work outbound.

The savings have to be large to make sense. You would likely arrive tired, pay for the same hotel night, and get little or no beach time Thursday. With three travelers and only three nights, the morning nonstop is the better value even if it costs a bit more.
Sunday early afternoon or late afternoon?

Late afternoon. Early afternoon makes checkout feel rushed and can erase the last pool or beach morning. A late-afternoon nonstop still gets you back to Atlanta in time to get home, unpack basics, and be ready for Monday, assuming it is not a very late evening arrival.
I'm nervous paid breakfast adds up.

Fair. Before booking, confirm whether the room has a mini-fridge and what the coffee setup is. Then plan one grocery delivery or quick stop for yogurt, fruit, snacks, and drinks. Use paid breakfast selectively, not every morning. If the resort breakfast is expensive and there is no fridge, the suite becomes more competitive.
What about the rental car?

For the Gulf-side hotel, skip a full-trip rental for now. Use an airport transfer or rideshare and walk to dinners. Add a one-day rental only if you decide on an off-beach outing. If you switch to the inland suite, rent a car from the start.
Should I hold now or wait until tomorrow?

Hold or book the cancellable hotel now if the rate is good; those beach rates can move quickly. For flights, book if the fare is not basic economy and changes are manageable. Waiting only makes sense if you still need to verify the hotel's cancellation deadline, resort fee, and room setup.
Okay, give me the version to book and the gotchas.

Book or hold: Thursday morning ATL-TPA nonstop in economy; Sunday late-afternoon TPA-ATL nonstop; cancellable Gulf-side room with pool and walkable restaurants; no full-trip rental car. Choose seats together first, and take a no-fee window if one fits the seating plan. Gotchas to verify before final payment: resort fee and taxes, breakfast prices, mini-fridge, bed setup, pool or beach access restrictions, cancellation deadline, weather-season policy, parking cost if you later add a car, and the booster-seat plan for airport transfers.
